## PACKING TIMELINE, ROOM-BY-ROOM CHECKLIST & DECLUTTER TIPS

### The Cross-Country Declutter Rule
Long-distance moves are priced by **weight and cubic feet**. Every pound costs money. 
* **The $1/Pound Rule:** Full-service movers average roughly $0.75–$1.00 per pound for a cross-country trip. Ask yourself: *"Would I pay $50 to ship this $40 IKEA bookshelf to Oregon?"* If no, sell or donate it.
* **Liquids & Heavy Consumables:** Do not pack canned goods, bulk pantry items, half-empty cleaning bottles, or old paint/liquids (movers legally cannot take flammables/aerosols anyway). 

### Room-by-Room Packing Checklist (Weeks 6 to 1)
*Color-code boxes by room with colored duct tape, and number every box (keep a master note on your phone of what's inside Box #1, Box #2, etc.).*

**Storage, Garage & Closets (Weeks 5–6)**
- [ ] **J** Purge tools, sports gear, and holiday decor.
- [ ] **M** Drain fuel and oil from any gas-powered lawn tools (movers won’t take them with fuel).
- [ ] **P** Pack out-of-season clothes in vacuum-seal bags or wardrobe boxes.

**Guest Room, Office & Decor (Weeks 3–4)**
- [ ] **J** Take down wall art, mirrors, and frames; wrap in picture boxes.
- [ ] **J** Pack books in *small* boxes only (so they don't get too heavy to lift or crush the bottom).
- [ ] **P** Back up computers to the cloud or an external hard drive. Photograph the back of your TV/desk setup so you remember how cords plug in.

**Living Room & Bedrooms (Weeks 2–3)**
- [ ] **J** Disassemble bulky furniture (bed frames, bookshelves). Put screws/bolts into labeled Ziploc bags and **tape them securely to the furniture piece** (or keep all hardware in one master "Parts Box").
- [ ] **J** Pack extra linens, towels, and pillows (use them as padding for fragile items).

**Kitchen & Bathrooms (Weeks 1–2)**
- [ ] **J** Set aside 1 week's worth of paper plates, cups, and plastic utensils, plus 1 pot and 1 pan. Pack the rest.
- [ ] **J** Pack plates **vertically** (like records) with plenty of packing paper; they are much less likely to break than when stacked flat.
- [ ] **P** Put plastic wrap under the caps of any toiletries you *are* taking to prevent leaks in changing elevations.

---

## DOG-SPECIFIC CROSS-COUNTRY CHECKLIST

Driving ~2,400 miles takes 4 to 5 days at a comfortable pace (8–9 hours of driving per day).

**4–6 Weeks Out**
- [ ] **M** **Vet Visit:** Get a physical print-out and digital PDF of rabies certificate, vaccine history, and heartworm/flea prevention. Ask for a 2-month supply of regular meds.
- [ ] **M** **Anxiety/Motion Sickness:** If your dog stresses in the car, ask the vet for a mild sedative (like Trazodone or Gabapentin) or anti-nausea meds (Cerenia), and **test a dose at home** before the trip to see how they react.
- [ ] **M** **Acclimate:** If using a new travel crate or crash-tested harness, start getting the dog used to it now with treats.

**2 Weeks Out**
- [ ] **P** **Book Pet-Friendly Hotels:** Look at La Quinta, Kimpton, Residence Inn, or Best Western (check weight limits and pet fees on BringFido.com). Request ground-floor rooms near exits for easy late-night potty breaks.
- [ ] **M** **Temp ID Tag:** Make a cheap $5 pet tag at a pet store with your cell numbers and the words *"Moving to OR"* or a relative's backup number.

**During the Drive & Arrival**
- [ ] **J** Keep the dog's feeding schedule strictly the same as home. Bring a 1–2 gallon jug of **home tap water** (sudden water changes across states can cause an upset stomach).
- [ ] **J** Never leave the dog unattended in the car; do drive-thru food or take turns going into rest stops.
- [ ] **J** **Arrival:** Before letting the dog loose in the new Oregon home/yard, check all fence latches, gates, and screens, and set up their bed/toys first so the space smells familiar.

---

## TIMELINE FOR CANCELLING & STARTING SERVICES

**4 Weeks Out (Notify / Cancel)**
- [ ] **J** Gym memberships, local clubs, or co-working spaces (many require 30 days' in-person or written notice).
- [ ] **J** Lawn care, pest control, house cleaning, or snow removal in Ohio.

**2 Weeks Out (Transfer / Schedule)**
- [ ] **M** **Ohio Utilities (Schedule Shutoff for Day *After* Move):** Electric, gas, water/sewer, trash, internet.
- [ ] **M** **Oregon Utilities (Schedule Start for Day *Before* Arrival):** Electric, gas, water, trash, internet.
- [ ] **P** **USPS Mail Forwarding:** Submit online at usps.com.
- [ ] **P** **Prescriptions:** Transfer recurring prescriptions to a national pharmacy chain (Walgreens, CVS, Costco) near your new Oregon address.
- [ ] **J** **Auto & Home/Renters Insurance:** Set policy transfer dates so there is zero gap in coverage.

**1 Week Out & Post-Move (Update Address)**
- [ ] **J** Employer HR / Payroll (crucial for switching from Ohio to Oregon state income tax withholding).
- [ ] **J** Banks, credit cards, Venmo/PayPal, student loans, and auto loans.
- [ ] **J** **Shopping Apps:** Delete your Ohio default address from Amazon, Target, Chewy, and food delivery apps so you don't accidentally ship things to your old house!
- [ ] **J** Streaming services (Hulu Live/YouTube TV need your new zip code for local channels).

---

## 8-WEEK PHONE CALENDAR REMINDERS
*Copy and paste these into your shared phone calendar (set alerts for Sunday mornings at 10:00 AM):*

* **Week 8 Out:** `[MOVE] Book Mover/Truck + Lock in Oregon Housing + Schedule Dog Vet Visit`
* **Week 7 Out:** `[MOVE] Gather Vital Documents Folder + Plan Driving Route & Book Pet Hotels`
* **Week 6 Out:** `[MOVE] Give 60/30-Day Lease Notice + Buy Packing Supplies + Declutter Garage/Closets`
* **Week 5 Out:** `[MOVE] Book Oregon Internet Install + Get Car Serviced for Cross-Country Drive`
* **Week 4 Out:** `[MOVE] Cancel Local Gyms/Subscriptions + Pack Guest Room, Books & Out-of-Season Clothes`
* **Week 3 Out:** `[MOVE] Schedule OH Utility Shutoffs & OR Utility Starts + Transfer Auto/Renters Insurance`
* **Week 2 Out:** `[MOVE] File USPS Mail Forwarding + Confirm Mover/Truck Details + Pack Living Room/Decor`
* **Week 1 Out:** `[MOVE] Pack Kitchen + Defrost Fridge (24h prior) + Pack Car Bags & Dog Travel Kit`

# 📋 PRINTABLE: MOVING DAY & ROAD TRIP ESSENTIALS
**Keep Every Item Below in Your Car — DO NOT Put on the Moving Truck!**

### 1. The "VIP" Folder (Front Seat / Backpack)
- [ ] Driver’s licenses, passports, Social Security cards, birth/marriage certificates
- [ ] Cash ($200–$500 in small bills for mover tips, tolls, or emergencies) + 2 physical credit cards
- [ ] New Oregon lease/closing docs + landlord/realtor phone numbers
- [ ] Moving company contract, inventory list, and driver’s cell number
- [ ] Vehicle title, current registration, and printed auto insurance card
- [ ] Dog's printed rabies certificate, vaccine records, and vet medications

### 2. The Dog’s Road Trip Bag (Easy Reach in Backseat)
- [ ] Crash-tested harness/seatbelt tether or secured crate
- [ ] 7–10 days of dog food in an airtight bin + high-value treats
- [ ] 1–2 gallons of home tap water + collapsible travel bowls
- [ ] Primary leash + **1 backup leash** (in case one snaps or gets lost at a rest stop)
- [ ] Poop bags, paper towels, pet-safe enzymatic cleaner, and old towels (for muddy paws/car sickness)
- [ ] Favorite blanket and 2–3 toys (unwashed, so they smell like home)
- [ ] Daily meds, calming chews/sedatives, and pet first-aid supplies

### 3. Human Road Trip & "First Night" Box
- [ ] 5–7 days of comfortable clothes, layers for Oregon weather, and toiletries
- [ ] Daily medications + basic first-aid kit (Ibuprofen, bandages, antacids)
- [ ] Phone chargers, car charging cables, and 1–2 portable power banks
- [ ] **First Night Bedding:** 1 set of sheets, pillows, and blankets (or air mattress + pump if arriving before the truck)
- [ ] **First Night Bathroom:** 2 rolls of toilet paper, hand soap, shower curtain + liner, and 2 bath towels
- [ ] **First Night Home:** Paper towels, trash bags, scissor/box cutter, basic toolkit (screwdriver/allen wrench), flashlights, paper plates, and plastic utensils

### 4. Car Emergency Kit (Trunk)
- [ ] Spare tire (checked for pressure), jack, and jumper cables / jump-start battery pack
- [ ] Tire pressure gauge and portable air compressor
- [ ] Windshield scraper, extra washer fluid, and 1 quart of motor oil
- [ ] Case of bottled water and non-perishable road snacks

### 5. Final Walk-Through Before Locking the Door in Ohio
- [ ] Walk every room, closet, cabinet, dishwasher, washer/dryer, basement, and garage
- [ ] Take timestamped photos/video of empty, clean rooms (for security deposit proof)
- [ ] Take photos of final electric, gas, and water meter readings
- [ ] Set thermostat to landlord/buyer specifications; turn off all lights and water valves
- [ ] Leave keys, garage openers, and forwarding address as instructed — **Hit the road to Oregon!**
